newsitem.title: UK: UK's Channel 5 says hits initial retuning target.
newsitem.headline: UK's Channel 5 says hits initial retuning target.

text.p: The UK's Channel 5, set to launch this month, claims it has met its initial retuning target, the Independent Television Commission, said on Wednesday.

An ITC spokeswoman said that Channel 5 had notified it that it had met its target of retuning 90 percent of homes in its initial transmission area which may suffer interference from the new station's signal.
The spokeswoman said the ITC was now verifying the claim and expected to make an announcement in the next few days.
Channel 5, the first terrestrial television station to be launched in Britain since 1982, goes on air on March 30.

It expects to be available to around 40 million people - some 65 percent of the UK population - at launch. It hopes to boost this to 45-46 million by the end of the year as an extra broadcasting frequency comes into play.
Channel 5 has spent some 150 million pounds on retuning in homes where video, cable or satellite reception could be affected by its signal.
The new channel is owned by Pearson Plc, United News & Media Plc, European broadcast group CLT-Ufa and U.S investment firm Warburg Pincus.
